name: Ganga
mouth: Bay of Bengal (Meghna estuary / Sundarbans Delta)
interStateSignificance: Lifeline of north India supporting ~43% of India's population; subject of National Ganga River Basin Authority & Namami Gange programme.
examFacts: National River of India, declared in November 2008.
Formed by the sacred confluence of the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda rivers at Devprayag in Uttarakhand.
The Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta is the largest river delta in the world.
Possesses unique self-purifying property historically attributed to high bacteriophage concentration and dissolved oxygen retention.
National Waterway 1 (NW-1), the longest operational national waterway in India (1,620 km), runs from Prayagraj to Haldia on the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly system.

name: Brahmaputra
origin: Chemayungdung Glacier near Mount Kailash & Lake Manasarovar, Tibet
sourceLocation: Angsi / Chemayungdung Glacier, southwestern Tibet (elevation ~5,300 m)
directionOfFlow: Eastward in Tibet, South into India, then West through Assam, South into Bay of Bengal
mouth: Bay of Bengal (unites with Ganga/Padma and Meghna in Bangladesh)
interStateSignificance: Crucial international braided river sharing borders with China, India, Bhutan, and Bangladesh.
examFacts: Known as the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet; makes a dramatic hairpin turn at Namcha Barwa (7,782 m) to enter India through the Great Yarlung Tsangpo Gorge.
Called Siang / Dihang upon entering Arunachal Pradesh; becomes the Brahmaputra after joining the Dibang and Lohit at Kobo near Sadiya.
Houses Majuli, the world's largest inhabited freshwater river island (first island district of India, declared 2016).
Has the highest discharge volume of any river in India and is notorious for massive monsoon sediment load and shifting sandbars (braided pattern).
National Waterway 2 (NW-2) spans 891 km on the Brahmaputra between Sadiya and Dhubri.

name: Indus
origin: Bokhar Chu glacier near Lake Manasarovar, Tibet
sourceLocation: Bokhar Chu (Singi Khamban - Lion's Mouth, elevation ~5,182 m)
directionOfFlow: Northwest through Ladakh, turns south around Nanga Parbat into Pakistan, drains into Arabian Sea
interStateSignificance: Governed by the historic Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) of 1960 brokered by the World Bank between India and Pakistan.
examFacts: Under the Indus Waters Treaty (1960), the waters of the three 'Eastern Rivers' (Sutlej, Beas, Ravi) were allocated exclusively to India, while the three 'Western Rivers' (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) were allocated to Pakistan, with India permitted run-of-the-river hydroelectric generation and limited non-consumptive usage.
The Indus flows exclusively through the Union Territory of Ladakh within India before entering Pakistan-administered territories.
Flanked by the Ladakh Range to the north and the Zanskar Range to the south in its upper course.
Cradled the ancient Indus Valley Civilization (Harappan Civilization), one of the world's earliest bronze-age urban cultures.
Enters India near Demchok in southeastern Ladakh.

name: Godavari
majorTributariesLeft: Pranahita (formed by confluence of Wardha, Penganga, and Wainganga - largest tributary)
mouth: Bay of Bengal (splits into Gautami Godavari and Vasishta Godavari near Rajahmundry)
interStateSignificance: Longest river of Peninsular India, often called 'Dakshin Ganga' or 'Vridha Ganga'.
examFacts: Second longest river in India after the Ganga and the largest river basin in Peninsular India (nearly 9.5% of India's total geographical area).
Pranahita is the largest tributary of the Godavari, formed by the combined waters of the Wardha, Penganga, and Wainganga rivers.
Sir Arthur Cotton constructed the Dowleswaram Barrage across the Godavari in 1852, transforming the drought-prone delta into the fertile 'Rice Bowl of Andhra Pradesh'.
Polavaram National Irrigation Project in Andhra Pradesh is designed to provide inter-basin water transfer from Godavari to Krishna basin via the Polavaram Right Main Canal.
Kaleshwaram Project in Telangana is recognized as the world's largest multi-stage lift irrigation project on the Godavari River.

name: Krishna
mouth: Bay of Bengal at Hamsaladeevi, Andhra Pradesh
interStateSignificance: Second largest east-flowing peninsular river; subject of decades-long Krishna Water Disputes Tribunals (KWDT I & II).
examFacts: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam on the Krishna River (border of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh) is one of the world's largest masonry dams.
Tungabhadra is the largest right-bank tributary of the Krishna, formed by the union of the Tunga and Bhadra rivers at Koodli near Shivamogga, Karnataka.
Prakasam Barrage at Vijayawada creates a massive road-cum-regulator across the Krishna delta.
The Koyna earthquake of 11 December 1967 (magnitude 6.3) is one of the world's classic examples of Reservoir-Induced Seismicity (RIS).
Musi River, on whose banks the historic city of Hyderabad was founded by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah in 1591, is a left-bank tributary of the Krishna.

name: Kaveri
origin: Talakaveri in Brahmagiri Range, Kodagu (Coorg), Karnataka
majorDams: Grand Anicut (Kallanai - built by Karikala Chola)
mouth: Bay of Bengal at Poompuhar (Kaveripoompattinam), Tamil Nadu
interStateSignificance: Known as 'Ponni' in Tamil literature; subject of historic Kaveri Water Disputes Tribunal (CWDT) and Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA).
examFacts: Unlike most peninsular rivers which are strictly seasonal, the Kaveri receives rainfall in both the South-West Monsoon (in upper Karnataka catchment) and the North-East Retreating Monsoon (in lower Tamil Nadu catchment), maintaining flow throughout most of the year.
Grand Anicut (Kallanai), constructed across the Kaveri by Chola King Karikala in the 2nd century CE, is one of the oldest functioning water-diversion dams in the world.
Shivanasamudra Falls on the Kaveri River in Mandya, Karnataka was the site of Asia's first major hydroelectric power station, established in 1902 to supply electricity to the Kolar Gold Fields (KGF).
The Kaveri forms three prominent river islands on its course: Srirangapatna, Shivanasamudra, and Srirangam, all hosting ancient Ranganathaswamy Vaishnavite temples.
Hogenakkal Falls on the Kaveri along the Karnataka-Tamil Nadu border is often referred to as the 'Niagara Falls of South India'.

name: Narmada
origin: Amarkantak Plateau, Anuppur district, Madhya Pradesh
majorDams: Indira Sagar Dam (largest reservoir in MP)
mouth: Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea) near Bharuch
interStateSignificance: Longest west-flowing peninsular river in India, flowing through a tectonic rift valley between Vindhya and Satpura ranges.
examFacts: Flows westward through a structural rift valley fault between the Vindhya Range to the north and the Satpura Range to the south.
Dhuandhar Falls ('Smoke Cascade') and the Marble Rocks canyon at Bhedaghat near Jabalpur are iconic geological features on the upper Narmada.
Forms an estuary rather than a delta at its mouth near Bharuch due to steep gradient, rapid flow, and lack of extensive deltaic sediment deposition in the tidal rift zone.
Sardar Sarovar Dam at Kevadia in Gujarat is the centerpiece of the Narmada Valley Project and powers the massive Narmada Main Canal supplying water to Saurashtra, Kutch, and Rajasthan.
Narmada Parikrama is an ancient circumambulatory pilgrimage where devotees walk ~2,600 km along both banks from origin to mouth and back.

name: Tapi
origin: Multai in the Betul district, Satpura Range, Madhya Pradesh
majorDams: Ukai Dam (Vallabh Sagar - 2nd largest reservoir in Gujarat)
mouth: Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea) near Surat (Dumas)
interStateSignificance: Twin river to the Narmada, flowing almost parallel to it south of the Satpura Range in its own rift valley.
examFacts: Often referred to as the 'Handmaid of the Narmada' because it flows westward in a parallel trough south of the Satpura Range.
Ukai Dam across the Tapi River in Tapi district, Gujarat features an enormous earth-cum-masonry dam with an installed capacity of 300 MW.
Kakrapar Atomic Power Station in Gujarat draws its cooling water from the Tapi River / Kakrapar reservoir system.
Surat, the global diamond cutting capital and historic textile port of the Mughal Empire, is situated on the lower course of the Tapi.
Burhanpur on the Tapi in Madhya Pradesh was the historic Mughal gateway to the Deccan and the original resting place of Mumtaz Mahal before her remains were transferred to the Taj Mahal.

name: Mahanadi
origin: Dhamtari district near Sihawa, Raipur hills, Chhattisgarh
majorDams: Hirakud Dam (longest earthen dam in the world)
mouth: Bay of Bengal at False Point / Paradip, Odisha
interStateSignificance: Lifeline of Odisha and Chhattisgarh; historically known as the 'Sorrow of Orissa' prior to Hirakud Dam construction.
examFacts: Hirakud Dam built across the Mahanadi near Sambalpur, Odisha is one of the longest dams in the world (main dam 4.8 km, total dyke system 25.8 km).
Cuttack, the ancient millenary silver city of Odisha, sits on the spit of land formed by the Mahanadi and its southern distributary, the Kathajodi.
Mahanadi Delta is an intricate network of distributaries (Kathajodi, Kuakhai, Daya, Bhargavi) draining into the Bay of Bengal and feeding the northern rim of Chilika Lake.
Rajim at the confluence of Mahanadi, Pairi, and Sondhur rivers in Chhattisgarh is celebrated as the 'Prayag of Chhattisgarh' and hosts the Rajim Kumbh Mela.

The Mahanadi Water Disputes Tribunal was constituted by the Central Government in March 2018 under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 to adjudicate water-sharing disputes between Odisha and Chhattisgarh.
